records.text: After Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian who came from the land of Kittim, had defeated Darius king of the Persians and Medes, he became king in his place, having first ruled over Greece.
He waged many wars, took possession of strongholds, and slaughtered kings of the earth.
He gathered an exceedingly strong army and ruled over countries, nations, and rulers; they became tributary to him.
After this he fell upon his bed and knew that he was dying.
Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
His officers took power, each in his own place.
They all put on diadems after his death, and their sons after them for many years; they multiplied evils on the earth.
Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of My anger and wrath is in their hands.
I will send My anger against a lawless nation, and I will command My people to take spoils and plunder, trample the cities and reduce them to dust.
But he did not consider it this way and has not reckoned it this way in his soul; rather, his mind will turn aside, even to destroy not a few nations.
If they say to him, “You alone are ruler,”
he will say, “Did I not take the country above Babylon and Chalanneh, where the tower was built? I also took Arabia, Damascus and Samaria.
As I took these in my hand, I will also take all the dominions. Wail, carved images in Jerusalem and Samaria!
For as I did to Samaria and her handmade objects, so I will also do to Jerusalem and her idols.”
Will an ax be glorified without the one cutting with it, or a saw be raised without the one drawing it? Likewise, if someone lifts a rod or a piece of wood.
In the first year of King Cyrus, he told me to be strong and take courage.

“Now I have come to show you the truth. Three kings have stood in opposition in Persia, and the fourth will become richer than all the others. When he grows strong through his wealth, he will rise against every king of the Greeks.
A powerful king will arise, exercise great lordship, and do whatever he wishes.

When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or the lordship with which he ruled. His kingdom will be removed, and he will teach others these things.
He will strengthen Egypt’s kingdom, and one of the rulers will overpower him and rule; his rule will be a great rule.
The Lord turned to destroy Daughter Zion’s wall. He stretched out a measure; He did not withdraw His hand from trampling. The outer defense mourned, and the wall weakened together with it.
Her gates were fixed in the earth; He destroyed and broke her bars. Her king and her rulers are among the nations. There is no law; even her prophets saw no vision from the Lord.
My eyes failed with tears; my heart was troubled. My glory was poured onto the ground at the shattering of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child failed in the city’s squares.
They said to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” They weakened like the wounded in the city’s squares, and their lives poured out into their mothers’ bosoms.
Thus says the Lord: “Because Zion’s daughters were exalted and walked with high neck and glancing eyes, dragging their tunics as their feet moved and playing with their feet,
God will humble Zion’s ruling daughters, and the Lord will uncover their appearance
on that day, and the Lord will remove the glory of their clothing and their ornaments, hair braids, fringes and crescents,
the necklace and the adornment of their face,
the arrangement of glorious adornment, armlets, bracelets, a hair braid, armbands, rings and earrings,
the garments bordered with purple and those purple at the center,
the coverings used about the house and the transparent Laconian garments,
the fine-linen, blue-purple and scarlet garments, and fine linen interwoven with gold and blue-purple, and trailing summer wraps.
Your most beautiful son, whom you love, will fall by the sword, and your strong men will fall by the sword.
The cases of your adornment will be humbled and mourn; you will be left alone and dashed to the ground.”
After striking Egypt, Antiochus returned in the one hundred and forty-third year. He went up against Israel and came up to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
He arrogantly entered the sanctuary and took the golden altar, the lampstand for light and all its utensils,
the table of presentation, the libation vessels, the bowls, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the gold ornament on the front of the temple. He stripped everything off.
He took the silver, the gold, the precious vessels, and the hidden treasures that he found.
Having taken everything, he went away to his own land. He committed bloodshed and spoke with great arrogance.
Great mourning came upon Israel in every place where they lived.
The earth shook over its inhabitants, and the whole house of Jacob put on shame.
After two full years, the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah. He came to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, he built an abomination of desolation upon the altar. They built pagan altars in the surrounding cities of Judah.
Whenever a book of the covenant was found in someone’s possession, or anyone consented to the law, the king’s decree put him to death.
By their power they dealt in this way with Israelites found in the cities, month after month.
On the twenty-fifth day of the month they offered sacrifice on the pagan altar that stood upon the altar.
And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy was found among Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem.

They returned to the injustices of their earlier fathers, who would not listen to My words; and behold, they walk after foreign gods to serve them. And the house of Israel and the house of Judah shattered My covenant that I established with their fathers.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people from which they will not be able to escape; and they will cry to Me, and I will not listen to them.
And you, do not pray for this people or petition for them with supplication and prayer, because I will not listen when they call upon Me, in their time of affliction.
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the Lord’s word came to me:

Take a writing roll and write on it all the words I have delivered to you as oracles concerning Jerusalem, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah until today.
Perhaps Judah’s house will hear all the calamities I intend to bring upon them, so that they turn from their evil way and I may be merciful toward their injustices and sins.
Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and he wrote on a writing roll, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the Lord’s words which He had delivered to him as oracles.
Jeremiah instructed Baruch, I am under guard and cannot enter the Lord’s house.
Read from this roll in the people’s hearing at the Lord’s house on a fast day, and read it to all Judah’s people coming from their city.
Perhaps their appeal for mercy will fall before the Lord, and they will turn from their evil way, for great are the Lord’s wrath and anger which He has pronounced against this people.
Baruch did everything Jeremiah instructed him, reading the Lord’s words from the document in the Lord’s house.
They entered the court to see the king, leaving the roll for safekeeping in Elishama’s house, and reported all the words to the king.
The king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll. He took it from Elishama’s house, and Jehudi read it to the king and all the rulers standing around him.
The king was sitting in a winter house, with a fire brazier before him.
Neither the king nor his servants who heard all these words sought anything or tore their garments.
Elnathan, Gedaliah, and Gemariah advised the king not to burn the roll.
The king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. But they were hidden.
After the king burned the roll—all the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth—the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
Take another roll again and write all the words that were on the roll which King Jehoiakim burned.
Say, Thus said the Lord: You burned this roll, saying, Why did you write in it that Babylon’s king will certainly enter and destroy this land, and people and animals will cease from it?
Therefore thus said the Lord concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one sitting on David’s throne. His carcass will be thrown out in the day’s heat and the night’s frost.
I will visit him, his family, and his servants, and bring upon them, Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and Judah’s land all the calamities I pronounced to them, but they did not listen.
Baruch took another roll and wrote on it, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words of the document Jehoiakim burned. Still more words like these were added to it.
His son Judas, called Maccabeus, arose in his place.
All his brothers and everyone who had joined his father helped him, and they fought Israel’s war with gladness.
He spread glory for his people, put on a breastplate like a giant, and girded himself with his weapons of war; he waged battles, shielding the army with his sword.
In his deeds he was like a lion, like a young lion roaring over prey.
He searched out and pursued the lawless, and burned those who troubled his people.
The lawless shrank back from fear of him; all workers of lawlessness were shaken, and deliverance prospered in his hand.
He passed through the cities of Judah, destroyed the ungodly out of her, and turned wrath away from Israel.
His name reached to the end of the earth, and he gathered those who were perishing.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son is grief to his mother.
Treasures will not profit lawless people, but righteousness will rescue from death.
The Lord will not starve a righteous life, but He will overturn the life of the impious.
Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the courageous make rich.
A disciplined son will be wise, and he will use the foolish one as a servant.
An intelligent son was preserved from scorching heat, but a lawless son is ruined by wind at harvest.
The Lord’s blessing is upon the head of the righteous, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the impious.
One wise in heart will receive commands, but the unrestrained person who twists things with his lips will be tripped up.
One who walks sincerely walks confidently, but one who perverts his ways will be known.
One who signals with his eyes deceitfully gathers griefs for people, but one who reproves with frankness makes peace.
They sounded the trumpets and cried out with a loud voice.
After this Judas appointed leaders of the people: commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
He told those building houses, those betrothed to wives, those planting vineyards, and the fearful to return, each to his own house, according to the law.
